blurb: Neutral, spherical and hyperbolic geometry: models, PSL(2,ℝ), trigonometry, Fuchsian groups and Gauss–Bonnet.

pics.alt: Oil portrait of Nikolai Lobachevsky in a dark coat with a decoration at his collar
pics.caption: Nikolai Lobachevsky (1792–1856), portrait by Lev Kryukov from the first half of the 19th century. Lobachevsky presented his hyperbolic geometry at Kazan University in 1826 and published it in 1829–1830.
pics.title: Lobachevsky.jpg

pics.alt: Poincaré disk with many thin circular arcs through one point, none of which meets a thick blue arc
pics.caption: The Poincaré disk model: geodesics are arcs of circles orthogonal to the boundary circle. Infinitely many geodesics (thin arcs) pass through one point without meeting the blue geodesic, so the parallel postulate fails.
pics.title: Poincare disc hyperbolic parallel lines.svg
